title: Cross-SDK transport defaults, timeouts, and connection pooling with concrete examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: SDK users across Python, TypeScript, and Go see inconsistent defaults for HTTP transport, request timeouts, and connection pool/keep-alive tuning. This leads to: inadvertent connection churn, higher tail latency for short requests, accidental blocking on streaming reads, and unclear retry semantics. Goal: define a small, opinionated cross-SDK transport configuration surface + concrete examples so apps get reliable, efficient behavior out-of-the-box while keeping advanced knobs for platform users.
proposal: We will standardize a minimal transport configuration API across Python/TS/Go SDKs and ship docs + examples. Key decisions: 1) Expose a TransportConfig object that supports: connect_timeout, read_timeout (per-request overall), response_header_timeout, max_conns, max_idle_conns_per_host, idle_conn_timeout, keepalive (boolean), max_conns_per_host (Go-specific), and stream_timeout (applies to streaming read loop). 2) Provide safe defaults that favor low latency and connection reuse: connect_timeout=2000ms, read_timeout=60000ms for normal requests, response_header_timeout=5000ms, idle_conn_timeout=90s, max_conns=100, max_idle_conns_per_host=10. For streaming endpoints the SDK will not impose an overall read timeout by default but will surface stream_timeout (nil/0 means no SDK-enforced timeout). 3) Ensure retry semantics: non-streaming requests use idempotency-based retries with exponential backoff (max_retries=2 by default) and early detection for connection errors. Streaming requests are not retried automatically by default; SDKs will provide helper utilities for resumable streams when the server supports it. 4) Provide explicit examples for each language showing how to opt into keepalive pools and how to tune for high-concurrency low-latency workloads. 5) Add integration tests that assert connection reuse and measure reduced short-request P95. 6) Add migration guidance and a deprecation timeline for any existing incompatible knobs.
python_example:
# Python (httpx) example
from redwood import RedwoodClient, TransportConfig
import httpx

# Recommended default transport config
cfg = TransportConfig(connect_timeout_ms=2000, read_timeout_ms=60000, response_header_timeout_ms=5000, max_conns=100, max_idle_conns_per_host=10, idle_conn_timeout_s=90, keepalive=True, max_retries=2)
client = RedwoodClient(transport_config=cfg)

# Streaming usage: SDK will yield lines/chunks; do not set global read timeout if you expect long streams
with client.stream_completion(model='x-large', prompt='...') as stream:
    for chunk in stream.iter_chunks():
        process(chunk)

# If you need a custom underlying transport (advanced):
transport = httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=0)  # disable library-level retries if you want SDK-managed retries
custom_client = RedwoodClient(transport_config=cfg, httpx_transport=transport)
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs expose a consistent TransportConfig surface and docs
Default transport config is documented and used in SDK integration tests
Integration test demonstrates connection reuse (Idle connections > 0 after 50 short requests) and 10-20% P95 latency improvement for small requests versus current baseline
Streaming ergonomics: SDK streaming iterators do not time out by default; documented guidance for stream_timeout and reconnection
Retries: non-streaming requests use idempotency-aware retries with backoff; streaming defaults to no-auto-retry
Migration guide created and included in SDK release notes with deprecation timeline for removed knobs
rollout_plan: 1) Implement TransportConfig API and shared spec in a design doc. 2) Implement in Python, TS, and Go in feature branches with safety flags. 3) Run integration suite against internal staging cluster to validate connection reuse and P95 improvements. 4) Publish docs and examples. 5) Gradually enable default in the next minor SDK release (sdk-2026.03), monitor telemetry for error spikes. 6) If issues occur, rollback via feature flag and notify customers via changelog and GitHub issues.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Initial design review: PM Priya Shah: please call out behavior for long-polling endpoints and add a snippet showing how to explicitly disable keepalive for devices with NAT timeouts.
2026-03-04 - Eng review: Liam Rodriguez: move default MaxConns down to 100 to avoid socket exhaustion in serverless environments; keep parameter for heavy clients.

2026-03-06 - Security review request posted: https://confluence.redwood/sdks/security-transport-checklist (ticketized)

2026-03-09 - PR opened (typescript): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/511
2026-03-10 - Bench results in staging: short-request P95 improved 18% with idle_conn_timeout tuning, no increase in 5xxs observed.
notes: Edge cases and follow-ups: 1) Mobile SDKs and heavily NATed environments may need shorter idle_conn_timeout and keepalive disabled to avoid NAT mapping issues; include explicit examples. 2) gRPC transports (if adopted later) will follow same default surface but map fields to gRPC keepalive and connection/channel settings. 3) We should add a small telemetry counter for 'reconnects per minute' to detect client misconfiguration. 4) Document interplay with Dedicated routing/fallbacks (e.g., when a request is routed to a different region keepalive won't help).
